title: Even the urge (Genesis Rabbah 9:7)
hook: "very good" includes the urge; without it no one would build a house or marry
tomorrow: the garden was all for Adam. so what was the one catch?

segments.voice: Yesterday: truth springs from the earth, planted rather than defeated. Today, something else God puts in the ground of a person.

The smell of a rival's new car. A coworker's promotion. The friend whose post blew up while yours sank. That little burn in the chest doesn't feel holy. Genesis closes its first chapter with God looking at everything: "and, behold, it was very good." Rabbi Nahman bar Samuel stops on that word very, and makes a claim that sounds almost wrong.
screen: `THAT BURN IN THE CHEST.` → `IT WAS VERY GOOD.` → `A CLAIM THAT SOUNDS WRONG.`

segments.voice: In Genesis Rabbah he says: good, that's the good urge. Very good, that's the yetzer hara, the urge usually called the evil one. Wait: the evil urge is very good? Yes, he answers. Without it, no one would build a house, marry, have children or open a business. And he brings Ecclesiastes, where the speaker watches people work and decides that all their labor and skill come from rivalry, one person with another. The yetzer hara here isn't a cartoon devil on your shoulder. It's drive: wanting, hunger, ambition, the itch to have what they have. Left alone, it wrecks things, which is why it keeps its name. But the midrash refuses to wish it away. A world without it would be calm and empty: no houses going up, no families, no shop on the corner. The Mishnah has a phrase for the other half: love God with all your heart, with both your urges. So the claim here is simple and strange. Even the urge belongs to very good. The fire under the pot can burn the house down. It also cooks dinner.
screen: `GOOD, AND VERY GOOD.` · `NO URGE, NO HOUSE.` · `RIVALRY BEHIND THE WORK.` · `THE FIRE THAT COOKS DINNER.` · then, large: `EVEN THE URGE IS GOOD.`

segments.voice: Make a fist, tight, and feel the heat and pressure build: that's the urge, all push. Hold it for a few breaths. Then open your hand slowly, palm up, and feel the same strength still there, in fingers that could now carry or build something. Rest in the open hand for the rest of the sit.
screen: `A FIST: ALL PUSH.` · `AN OPEN HAND: THE SAME STRENGTH.`

segments.voice: Even the urge: in Genesis Rabbah, very good includes the yetzer hara, the drive without which no one builds a house.
For the road: even the urge is good, in steady hands. That's day fifteen seventy-two, done.

howItsDone: Jewish teaching often speaks of the yetzer hara and the yetzer tov, the two urges; this midrash on Genesis 1:31 is a common text when people study how ambition and desire can serve good ends.

fork.setup: your little brother asks why he gets so jealous of his friends' stuff, and whether that makes him bad. what does this midrash give you to say?
options: that jealousy is wicked; hope it goes away and never comes back.
that the feeling is a drive; it can wreck things or build things.
that it's fine; whatever you want, you should go and get.
fork.reveal: Rabbi Nahman bar Samuel: very good means the urge too. without it, no one builds a house. it still needs steering.

original.note: Hebrew: the evil urge, the drive this midrash finds inside very good.

what it means: a midrash reads very good as including the urge, since without it no one would build or marry.
what a scholar hears: Genesis Rabbah 9:7, Rabbi Nahman bar Samuel on Genesis 1:31, with Ecclesiastes 4:4 on rivalry.
guess: the drive in us, part of what God called very good

chat.meaning: In Genesis Rabbah, very good includes the yetzer hara: without drive, no one would build, marry or work. It needs steering.

yetzer hara.meaning: the evil urge: drive, wanting, ambition

Rabbi Nahman bar Samuel.meaning: the sage who reads very good as the urge too

Ecclesiastes.meaning: a book of the Bible about work, time and meaning

Mishnah.meaning: the early collection of Jewish law the Talmud builds on

sources.ref: Genesis Rabbah 9:7 (Rabbi Nahman bar Samuel: 'very good' is the evil urge; without it no one would build, marry, have children or do business)

sources.quoted: and, behold, it was very good

notes: Genesis Rabbah 9:7 paraphrased: 'good' = the good urge, 'very good' = the evil urge, with the list (build a house, marry, have children, do business) and Ecclesiastes 4:4. Confirm the attribution to Rabbi Nahman bar Samuel (bar Nahman in some editions).
Mishnah Berakhot 9:5 (be-khol levavkha, bi-shnei yetzarekha) paraphrased. Confirm.
Senses shape: the practice is physical (a fist, then an open hand). The hook's 'rival's new car' etc. are everyday pictures, not claims.
